relevance_reason: Reports three unrelated patients with developmental and epileptic encephalopathy who carry novel heterozygous GRIN2D missense variants, adding to the cases that define DEE46.

findings.statement: Tsuchida et al. (2018) reported 3 unrelated patients with developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, characterized by severe developmental delay and intractable epilepsy. When they compared their 3 patients with the 2 previously reported patients who had GRIN2D variants, they found that all 5 had similar clinical features.
quotes: novel heterozygous GRIN2D missense variants in three unrelated patients with severe developmental delay and intractable epilepsy
We assessed the clinical features of our three cases and compared them to those of the two previously reported GRIN2D variant cases, and found that they all show similar clinical features.

findings.statement: Using whole exome sequencing, Tsuchida et al. (2018) identified novel heterozygous missense variants in the GRIN2D gene in 3 unrelated patients with developmental and epileptic encephalopathy. All of the altered residues were highly conserved across vertebrates and among the 4 GluN2 subunits. Based on structural analysis, the authors concluded that all 3 variants probably impair GluN2D function, either by affecting intersubunit interaction or by altering channel gating activity.
quotes: we identified by whole exome sequencing novel heterozygous GRIN2D missense variants in three unrelated patients with severe developmental delay and intractable epilepsy
All altered residues were highly conserved across vertebrates and among the four GluN2 subunits.
Structural consideration indicated that all three variants are probably to impair GluN2D function, either by affecting intersubunit interaction or altering channel gating activity.

relevance_reason: This paper first reports the de novo GRIN2D variant in children with epileptic encephalopathy. It also includes functional studies and a treatment response.

findings.statement: Li et al. (2016) reported 2 unrelated children with epileptic encephalopathy whose seizures were refractory to conventional antiepileptic medications. The older proband later developed refractory status epilepticus.
quotes: identified by exome and candidate panel sequencing in two unrelated children with epileptic encephalopathy
Because both individuals' seizures had proven refractory to conventional antiepileptic medications
The older proband subsequently developed refractory status epilepticus

findings.statement: In 2 unrelated children with epileptic encephalopathy, Li et al. (2016) used exome and candidate panel sequencing to identify a recurrent de novo heterozygous missense mutation in the GRIN2D gene, c.1999G>A (p.Val667Ile). The variant lies in the M3 transmembrane domain, which is involved in channel gating. GRIN2D had not previously been recognized to harbor disease-causing mutations.
quotes: we report a de novo recurrent heterozygous missense mutation-c.1999G>A (p.Val667Ile)-in a NMDAR gene previously unrecognized to harbor disease-causing mutations, GRIN2D, identified by exome and candidate panel sequencing in two unrelated children with epileptic encephalopathy
The resulting GluN2D p.Val667Ile exchange occurs in the M3 transmembrane domain involved in channel gating.

findings.statement: Li et al. (2016) found that the GRIN2D V667I mutation causes a gain of function. It increased glutamate and glycine potency 2-fold and channel open probability 6-fold, reduced sensitivity to negative modulators such as extracellular protons, and prolonged deactivation after glutamate removal. Cultured neurons transfected with the mutant cDNA showed dendritic swelling and cell death, which the authors suggested reflected excitotoxicity from NMDAR overactivation.
quotes: This gain-of-function mutation increases glutamate and glycine potency by 2-fold, increases channel open probability by 6-fold, and reduces receptor sensitivity to endogenous negative modulators such as extracellular protons.
Moreover, this mutation prolongs the deactivation time course after glutamate removal
Transfection of cultured neurons with human GRIN2D cDNA harboring c.1999G>A leads to dendritic swelling and neuronal cell death, suggestive of excitotoxicity mediated by NMDAR over-activation.

findings.statement: Li et al. (2016) first tested the mutant receptors' sensitivity to FDA-approved NMDAR antagonists. Both children were then treated with oral memantine, which led to mild to moderate improvement in seizure burden and development. The older proband's later refractory status epilepticus improved dramatically, both electrically and clinically, with ketamine and magnesium. The authors suggested that NMDAR antagonists may be useful as adjuvant therapy in individuals with GRIN2D gain-of-function mutations.
quotes: oral memantine was administered to both children, with resulting mild to moderate improvement in seizure burden and development
The older proband subsequently developed refractory status epilepticus, with dramatic electroclinical improvement upon treatment with ketamine and magnesium.
these results suggest that NMDAR antagonists can be useful as adjuvant epilepsy therapy in individuals with GRIN2D gain-of-function mutations
